cards.heading: simple vs compound interest
cards.body: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is simple interest — 10% APR on $1,000 earns $100/year, period. APY (Annual Percentage Yield) includes compounding — your interest earns interest. The more frequently you compound, the higher the APY.

cards.heading: the compounding formula
cards.body: APY = (1 + APR/n)^n - 1, where n is compounds per year. 10% APR compounded daily (n=365) gives 10.52% APY. Compounded continuously, it gives 10.52% APY via e^APR - 1. Small difference at low rates, huge at high rates.

cards.text: A 100% APR compounded daily becomes 171.5% APY. Always check if a protocol shows APR or APY — the difference can be massive at high rates.

cards.heading: how farms work
cards.body:
1. Deposit tokens into a liquidity pool → receive LP tokens.
2. Stake LP tokens in a farm contract.
3. Earn reward tokens (e.g., AERO, COMP) proportional to your share.
4. Harvest rewards and optionally compound back.

cards.text: Auto-compounding vaults (like Beefy or Yearn) automatically harvest and restake your rewards, saving gas and maximizing APY.

cards.heading: low risk, low reward
cards.body: Lending USDC on Aave: 3-8% APY. Your principal stays in dollars, smart contract risk is the main concern. Blue-chip protocols with years of track record and audits.

cards.heading: high risk, high reward
cards.body: LP farming a new memecoin pair: 200-1000%+ APY. But the token might drop 90%, IL can be devastating, and the smart contract might not be audited. The APY number is meaningless if your principal goes to zero.

cards.text: If an APY looks too good to be true, ask: where is the yield coming from? Real fees, or printed tokens? Sustainable yield comes from real economic activity.

cards.heading: why APY drops over time
cards.body: Most farm rewards come from token emissions — the protocol prints new tokens to attract liquidity. As more people farm, the same emissions are split among more stakers. Plus, farmers sell reward tokens, pushing prices down.

cards.heading: real yield vs emission yield
cards.body: Real yield comes from actual protocol revenue — trading fees, interest, liquidation penalties. Emission yield comes from token inflation. Real yield is sustainable; emission yield is a temporary incentive that dilutes token holders.

cards.text: A farm paying 500% APY in emissions is likely printing tokens faster than demand can absorb. Check the token's price chart — if it's trending down, your 'yield' is being offset by depreciation.

cards.heading: strategy types
cards.body: Delta-neutral: hedge price exposure, earn only fees/funding. Pair farming: provide LP with correlated assets (ETH/stETH) for low IL. Single-sided: lend stablecoins for safe yield. Each fits different risk appetites.

cards.heading: calculating net yield
cards.body: Net yield = farming APY - impermanent loss - gas costs - smart contract risk premium. A 20% APY farm with 8% IL and 2% gas overhead nets you ~10%. Always do the math before committing capital.

cards.text: The best strategy is the one you understand. Start with simple stablecoin lending, then gradually explore LP farming as you gain confidence.
